title: Sumomomo Momomo
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Momoko, only child of the super-strong Kuzuryuu martial-arts clan, is sent to marry Koushi Inuzuka, heir of a rival clan, so the family line can continue with a strong heir. Koushi gave up fighting after being beaten while protecting Momoko as a child and now studies law to become a prosecutor; assassins and rival fighters keep forcing him back into combat. A 12-volume ecchi martial-arts comedy (Yen Press blurb; Manga Bookshelf review).
life_message: It holds up finding the courage to stand up for yourself and the people you care about.

content.note: Martial-arts fights and assassins hunting Koushi (review; AniList Martial Arts, MangaUpdates Unrealistic Fighting); not graphic per review.
Assassination plots played mostly for comedy (review).

Reviewer calls the fan service 'troubling': Momoko's clothes keep slipping, detailed panty shot; arranged-marriage and heir plot; school setting, ages unstated (review; AniList/MangaUpdates Ecchi, MangaDex suggestive).
Not described; comedic insults likely (to verify).
Koushi's childhood trauma from a beating (review; MangaUpdates Childhood Trauma).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Clan rules and a father's orders set Momoko's path (blurb).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Rival clans, lineage and an heir drive the plot (blurb).

folkways.japan: Draws on Japanese martial-arts clan (ryuha) lineage and arranged-marriage conventions, alongside the oshikake nyobo (self-proclaimed bride) comedy trope.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer notes the story's message that avoiding a fight is cowardly, carried by plot; no preachiness noted (Manga Bookshelf).

personified.ideology: Law and reason instead of fighting
Clan lineage needs a strong male heir

delivery.note: Koushi's lawful pacifism is sympathetic but the plot pushes him back into combat.

winners_losers: Courage and loyalty in a fight win; Koushi's wish to avoid violence gives way. Clan tradition gets sympathy, though Momoko disproves her father's doubts about women.
